Citi Bike daily panel, 2013 to 2026

Every Citi Bike ride since launch, rolled up to daily volume, trip duration, straight-line distance and implied speed — with the system's price changes, expansions and fleet events marked on the time axis.

Marked events

Price changes are drawn as solid rules, everything else as light rules, and the days the system was shut as a shaded band. Each event links to its source and quotes the sentence that dates it; the flag says whether that is an exact effective date or only the month.

    Data. Ride-level Citi Bike data, aggregated here to a daily panel. Source files are the schema-normalized monthly parquet at s3://ctbk/normalized/, public derived data published by hudcostreets/ctbk.dev, which in turn derives from Citi Bike's own public trip history under the NYCBS Data Use Policy. None of that project's code is used here — only its published data. Months that mirror has not reached (September 2026 on) are read straight from Citi Bike's own monthly files and normalized here to the same rules; on August 2026, which both publish, the two give identical daily numbers. Weather is NOAA GHCN-Daily for Central Park (station USW00094728).

    • Distance is a straight line between docks, not the route ridden. It is a floor on the true distance, so implied speed is a floor on true speed. Both are comparable over time, but neither is a statement about how far or fast anyone actually went.
    • Speed excludes round trips and outliers. Rides returning to the same dock have ~zero straight-line distance and would drag the median toward zero, so the speed series uses only rides over 200 m lasting between 1 minute and 2 hours. A day whose median rests on fewer than 30 rides is left as a gap.
    • Days the system was shut count as zero rides and are shaded on every chart: the storms that closed it (January 2016, February and March 2017, February 2021, January and February 2026) and a maintenance weekend in March 2015. Durations across the spring and autumn clock changes are corrected for the lost or repeated hour.
    • Bike type does not exist before January 2020. Earlier rides are "not recorded", not "classic". Rider gender and birth year stop being published at the same date.
    • Citi Bike removes some rides before publishing — staff service trips, test-station trips and anything under 60 seconds. They are missing from every series here.
    • 30 September 2026 is short by under 1%. Citi Bike switched its month files from end date to start date in October 2026, so rides that started that evening and ended after midnight are in neither file.
    • Event dates vary in precision. Those flagged "month" in the list above are known only to the month and are drawn on the 1st.
